rationale: The target is Prolangs-C++/life, a small cellular-automaton simulation with hot nested loops over a game grid and no source available beyond IR, so the priority is strong data/control-flow disguise with tight overhead. SUB gets the highest Runtime/Size/Correctness weights because instruction substitution is nearly free and safe in arithmetic-heavy kernels. FLA is weighted high on Security/Diversity since flattening the simulation's update loops is the main barrier to static analysis, with a deliberately low RuntimeCost weight to reflect that its dispatcher overhead is tolerable only in this small-hot-loop profile. BCF is kept moderate: opaque predicates resist the debugger well but inflate loops that run per-generation, so its RuntimeCost weight stays below SUB's. SPLIT is favored for diversity and correctness (it composes with FLA) at negligible cost. IBR and ICALL receive lower weights because this benchmark has few indirectable branches/calls and per-call indirection taxes the hot update path. IGV is kept moderate-low on CorrectnessRisk since life's global grid state is sensitive to aggressive global indirection, but moderate overall because hiding the grid representation is valuable to an analyst.
